name: Ring Flye
description: The ring flye is an advanced chest isolation exercise performed on gymnastic rings. With arms extended to the sides and elbows slightly bent, the athlete drives the hands together in a wide arc, creating intense pectoral stretch and contraction. The unstable nature of the rings demands significantly greater rotator cuff and serratus anterior activation compared to cable or dumbbell flyes.

execution.starting_position: Adjust rings to approximately chest height when standing. Grip one ring in each hand, lean forward, and extend arms out to the sides with a slight bend in the elbows. Body is inclined forward, weight on the balls of the feet.
execution.setup_instructions: Set gymnastic rings at a height where your body angle creates appropriate difficulty — lower rings make the exercise harder. Ensure rings are secured and level.
steps: Step 1: Begin with arms extended out to the sides, elbows slightly bent, body leaning forward at an angle determined by your strength level.
Step 2: Drive both hands together in a wide arc, maintaining the same elbow angle throughout — do not bend the elbows further.
Step 3: Squeeze the pectorals at the peak, hands meeting in front of your chest.
Step 4: Slowly reverse the motion, allowing the arms to open wide and stretch the chest under control.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale as you bring the rings together. Inhale during the controlled lowering phase.
common_mistakes: Bending the elbows excessively, turning it into a push-up
Losing body tension and sagging at the hips
Allowing rings to rotate outward at the top position
safety_considerations: This exercise places significant stress on the shoulder joint — ensure adequate rotator cuff strength before attempting
Start with a steeper body angle (more upright) to reduce difficulty and progress gradually
Never lock out elbows under load on rings
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Open arms as wide as comfortable without shoulder pain, aiming for a full pectoral stretch. Bring hands together at mid-chest level at the top.
coaching_cues: Hug a barrel — maintain the same arm shape throughout
Keep your chest proud and shoulders packed down away from ears
